h1: Banking and payment gateways for alcohol businesses
title: Banking and Payment Gateways for Alcohol | Craft Beer School
desc: How breweries and brewpubs in India can set up banking, card machines, UPI and payment gateways when alcohol is a restricted category.
teaser: Alcohol is a restricted category for many payment providers. Ask before you sign, not after the first settlement is held.
standfirst: Opening a current account and taking payments sounds routine until the provider sees the word alcohol. Some say no, some ask for more paperwork and some hold funds. Here is how to set up banking for a brewery or brewpub without surprises.
sections: Alcohol is a restricted category for many providers

Banks and payment companies classify merchants by risk. Alcohol sellers often sit in a restricted or higher-risk group, alongside other regulated trades. That does not mean you cannot get service. It means more questions at onboarding and, with some providers, a flat refusal for certain kinds of transaction.

The most common trouble comes from online payment gateways. Many list alcohol as a prohibited or restricted category for online sales, partly because selling alcohol online for delivery is not permitted in most Indian states. Card terminals and UPI at a licensed premises are usually far simpler.
Open the current account with paperwork ready

Your bank will want the usual company documents, plus proof that your business is licensed. Have these ready before the first meeting:

  • Certificate of incorporation or partnership deed, PAN and GST registration where applicable.
  • Copies of your excise licence or, if it is pending, the application and acknowledgement.
  • Your lease and a short description of what you sell and how.

Tell the bank clearly that you sell alcohol on a licensed premises. A relationship manager who knows this from the start can route your application properly. One who finds out later may freeze the account while compliance reviews it.
Card machines and UPI at the bar

For a brewpub, most payments will come through card terminals and UPI QR codes at the bar and tables. Ask your bank or terminal provider about these points before you sign:

  • Which merchant category your business will be coded under. Bars and pubs commonly sit under a drinking places category. The wrong code can trigger declines or reviews.
  • The merchant discount rate on cards and any charges on UPI.
  • Settlement timing: the next working day is common, but confirm it.
  • Whether tips can be added on the terminal and how they are settled.

Run test transactions with a few cards and UPI apps during your soft opening. Better to find a decline problem with friends than on a full Saturday night.
Online payments need a different conversation

Many brewpubs take online payments for things that are not alcohol sales: table deposits, event tickets, private party bookings, merchandise or gift vouchers. Some gateways will support these if the business is clear about what is being sold. Others refuse any merchant with an alcohol licence.

Be precise in the application. Describe exactly what will be sold online. Never route alcohol sales through a gateway that has approved you for something else. If the provider finds out, it can terminate the account and hold funds. Our guide to pricing private parties and corporate bookings covers deposits for events.

Many breweries run at least two bank accounts: one for daily trading and one for excise and tax payments. Moving the tax share of each day's takings into the second account means the money is there when duty falls due. Our guide to planning cash around excise payment dates sets out how.

For breweries selling kegs to other venues, set up clear payment terms and collect by bank transfer rather than cheque where possible. Payments from hotels and larger accounts often run on their own approval cycles. Our guide to selling to hotels covers what to expect.
Keep records that satisfy a compliance review

Every so often a bank or payment provider will review your account. Keep the excise licence current on file with them, update them when it renews and reconcile card and UPI settlements with your till daily. A brewpub that can show a clean match between its till, its settlements and its excise records answers a review quickly.

The daily reconciliation also catches problems in your own business: missing settlements, voided bills and staff errors.

Cash is the other side of this. Some guests still pay in notes. Count the cash drawer at every shift change, record it against the till and bank it regularly. Large unexplained cash deposits are exactly the kind of pattern that prompts a bank to ask questions about a licensed business. A clean daily record makes those questions short.

Your first step: before signing with any gateway or terminal provider, ask in writing whether they support licensed alcohol businesses and for which transaction types. Keep the reply on file.
faqs: Can a brewpub in India accept UPI and card payments?
Usually yes, through a bank or terminal provider that supports licensed alcohol businesses. Confirm the merchant category and settlement terms before signing.
Why do payment gateways refuse alcohol businesses?
Many classify alcohol as a restricted category, partly because online alcohol sales for delivery are not permitted in most Indian states.
Can a brewpub take online payments for event bookings?
Some gateways allow non-alcohol payments such as table deposits or tickets if you describe them accurately. Never route alcohol sales through an account approved for something else.
